correctness.summary: The path-blow-up counting identity is correct: distinct-layer endpoint pairs contribute the product of all layer sizes across their interval, while same-layer pairs have one geodesic through each adjacent-layer vertex. Independent exact evaluation for q=3,...,9 reproduces gpn(H_q)=121*3^q/36+33q/2-141/4 and the source equal-layer value 9*3^q/4+33q/2-81/4, with difference 10*3^(q-2)-15 in every case. The recurrence E_j=a_j(1+E_{j-1}) gives the general closed form used in the proof, so the infinite-family inequality does not depend on the finite verification script.

limitations: The family is not proved globally optimal, or even optimal among all path blow-ups for every order.
Only orders divisible by three are optimized in the stated theorem.
The universal upper bound from the source is not improved.
The source problem is very recent, so concurrency risk is high.

originality.summary: Knor-Sedlar-Skrekovski-Zhang's open-access 2026 paper introduces the invariant and explicitly poses Problem 14 asking for a graph with larger geodesic subpath number than G_{3,n/3} and/or a better upper bound. The audited tapered family exceeds that benchmark for every n=3q, q>=3. Current searches did not locate the same unequal-layer formula or tapered family. Because the invariant and problem are only months old, simultaneous or unindexed follow-up work remains a material priority risk.

scientific_value.summary: The construction settles the construction side of an explicit foundational open problem on an infinite sequence of orders and improves the leading constant by 121/81. The arbitrary path-blow-up formula is also a reusable exact tool for further extremal searches.
